indicators.value: GER rearm, delay 8 ticks
indicators.source: Hitler's memorandum on the Four-Year Plan, Aug 1936 (armed forces operational within four years; text in Treue, Vierteljahrshefte fuer Zeitgeschichte 1955) and the army armament programme of Aug 1936 (Deist, in Germany and the Second World War vol. I); two-year service decreed 24 Aug 1936; Tooze 2006
indicators.rule: the latest GER rearm decision. Note: realized_moves.csv tick 2. The memorandum and the army programme are dated to the month only; the date is that of the two-year service decree, the one exact date realized_moves.csv gives for this decision. With delay 8 the effect (arms_GER high) is visible at tick 11.

pending_GER_rearm.rule: pending_GER_rearm = max(0, d - (index(Q) - index(t))) = max(0, 8 - (10 - 2)) = 0: GER rearm decided 1936-08-24 (1936Q3, model tick 2) with delay d = 8, read at the end of Q = 1938Q3 (tick 11); the effect applied in the transition into tick 11 (the end of 1938Q3), so nothing is pending; the delay is the model's (docs/actions_ww2.md), hence medium

indicators.value: WEST rearm, delay 4 ticks

The French four-year programme of 7 Sep 1936 and the Defence Loans Act of 1937 fall under this pending decision (realized_moves.csv ticks 2 and 4): one WEST action stands for both governments' programmes (docs/actions_ww2.md). arms_WEST rising visible at tick 5.

pending_WEST_rearm.rule: pending_WEST_rearm = max(0, d - (index(Q) - index(t))) = max(0, 4 - (10 - 0)) = 0: WEST rearm decided 1936-03-03 (1936Q1, model tick 0) with delay d = 4, read at the end of Q = 1938Q3 (tick 11); the effect applied in the transition into tick 5 (the end of 1937Q1), so nothing is pending; the delay is the model's (docs/actions_ww2.md), hence medium

rearm_delay_ticks.basis: Provisional: the action catalogue's one-year lag from a rearmament decision to fielded force (docs/actions_ww2.md, rearm). NMC shows German military personnel rising from 461 to 596 thousand (1935 to 1936) in the year after conscription was reintroduced in March 1935, and British milex rising by 40 to 50 percent a year from 1936 to 1938 before the 1939 jump. To be refined by the historian from the programme records (Tooze 2006 for Germany; the Defence Requirements reports for Britain).
